source: Append-only synthesis of defect reports and controls in rounds 25-28. Each measurement records its date and command. Open work routes to round 30; historical observations are not represented as current failures. No rounds 8-28 files were changed.

entries.defect: The typed-pipeline gate's lossy legacy reconstruction manufactured derivation failures, while null-like owed slots were counted as present, producing a false red on typed D4 input.
entries.fix_scope: Round-25 typed-pipeline gate input-class and nullish-routing repair; historical manifests remain append-only.
entries.before: The typed D4 command exited 1 at 14/16: the reconstruction generated 8 DERIV-REPLAY failures and six phantom null routing slots.
entries.after: The declared-source typed D4 command exited 0 at 16/16 with no DERIV-REPLAY lines; the source packet remained 19/19 and the gate selftest reached 19/19.
entries.control: Independent cold rerun and post-fix typed-packet, source-packet, selftest, tamper, and frozen-generation controls; reports/round-25/gate-input/verify.md and reports/round-25/scribe/x46-gate-input-cold-rerun.md.
entries.owner_note: Closed by the cited bounded repair and controls. Preserve the pre-fix report as historical evidence; do not call the superseded red a current regression.

measurements.result: Pre-fix: exit 1, 14/16 legs, 8 manufactured DERIV-REPLAY failures, six phantom null slots; post-fix: exit 0, 16/16, zero DERIV-REPLAY lines.
Settled post-fix selftest: exit 0, 19/19.

entries.evidence: The pre-fix defect was in the gate's own reconstruction and null-like scalar handling. The repair graded the typed packet's pinned declared source and centralized nullish slot handling; the new frozen generation passed without rewriting historical manifests.

entries.defect: A single moved routing row can evade hold validation when its hold is null or absent; null is treated as a truthy string, and a missing hold disappears from both compared sets.
entries.owner_note: Add separate negative controls for a single null hold and a missing hold key; each must refuse or report the mismatch. Preserve the current clean and valid-null controls.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/typed-pipeline-gate.py <typed-D4 fixture with hold: null on one moved LEX-GAR row>
measurements.result: Exit 0, 16/16 despite a single laundered hold; nulling all moved rows is caught, so the single-row bypass is discriminating.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/typed-pipeline-gate.py <typed-D4 fixture with hold key absent on one moved row>
measurements.result: Exit 0, 16/16; the absent row drops out of both compared sets.

entries.evidence: These are pre-existing gaps, not regressions from the typed-input fix. Round-25's own selftest exercised deleted rows and renamed notes, not a single null or missing hold. No later cited control closes these cases.

entries.defect: Malformed typed-input paths can raise uncaught exceptions rather than the documented exit-2 could-not-evaluate result: a D4-shaped packet with a missing declared source crashes before the refusal branch, and a source-less typed packet with a routing row lacking record raises KeyError.
entries.owner_note: Guard source reads and semantic row access; add end-to-end malformed D4 and source-less typed fixtures that exit 2 without a traceback. The reported controls were historical probes, not a current re-run.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/typed-pipeline-gate.py <D4-shaped typed packet declaring a missing source>
measurements.result: Exit 1 with FileNotFoundError traceback instead of the promised named exit-2 refusal.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/typed-pipeline-gate.py <typed packet without typed_assembly and with a typed_channel row missing record>
measurements.result: Exit 1 with uncaught KeyError: 'record' instead of exit 2.

entries.evidence: The missing-source case was reproduced on both the pre-fix and landed gate; the missing-record case was reproduced on both the shipped gate and its predecessor. Neither is established as reachable from the committed packet shapes.

entries.defect: During the round-25 landing, the argot gate selftest had fixture/assertion failures and the typed-pipeline selftest temporarily crashed because owed_slot_of was not exported.
entries.fix_scope: Round-25 final gate and fixture revisions; no historical red is rewritten.
entries.before: Intermediate selftests failed while fixtures and module exports were landing.
entries.after: The settled argot and typed-pipeline controls both exited 0 with their final named checks passing.
entries.control: Final selftests and D4 runtime readings recorded in reports/round-25/scribe/fragment-ledger.md.
entries.owner_note: Closed as a transient integration state. Do not cite an intermediate red as the final gate state or erase its timing record.

measurements.result: Settled at 18/18, exit 0; earlier states included missing-fixture and failed-control readings.
Settled at 19/19, exit 0; an intermediate revision raised KeyError: 'owed_slot_of'.

entries.evidence: The final revision is green, but the in-flight failures explain why only settled revisions and their controls count as closure.

entries.defect: The predecessor replay engine modeled derivation as concatenation only, so correct reverse derivations were false failures and indistinguishable from incorrect reversals.
entries.fix_scope: Round-25 argot-derivation gate and paired positive/negative fixtures.
entries.before: A correct reverse and a wrong reverse produced byte-identical D-form-mismatch findings under the old engine.
entries.after: The new gate distinguished a correct reverse from a wrong operation and a tampered result; its fixture IDs matched the expected file.
entries.control: Argot gate selftest and positive/negative derivation fixtures; reports/round-25/audit/x47-argot-negatives.md.
entries.owner: Round-30 argot-gate owner (archive-only for this bounded class)
entries.owner_note: The old-engine false failure is closed by the new gate controls. This closure does not claim that the delivered D4 packet contains a derivation domain; see R25-ARGOT-REGISTER-RELATION-ABSENT.

measurements.result: 18/18 checks passed, exit 0.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/argot-derivation-gate.py <correct reverse fixture> and python3 tools/gates/argot-derivation-gate.py <wrong-operation fixture>
measurements.result: The correct pair passed; the wrong operation exited 1 with D4L-ARGOT-DERIV.

entries.evidence: The engine capability was repaired and independently exercised; the reported empty delivered relation is a separate coverage gap.

entries.defect: The D4 packet did not deliver the forecast register-derived relation, leaving the argot gate with no derived pair to grade; a green run therefore did not establish that the domain was checked.
entries.owner_note: Either deliver the declared register relation end-to-end or explicitly retain it as an undelivered delta. Do not infer coverage from an exit-zero run over an empty relation set.

measurements.result: Coverage reported derived_pairs=0 and violations=0; the clean exit was vacuous for derivation arithmetic.

entries.evidence: The same empty-relation limitation was re-measured in round 26 and retained as a named delta in round 27. The round-28 materials cited here do not establish that the relation later landed.

entries.defect: Several filed v3 handoff revisions repeated stale D4 claim prose after the family-clean change; the round-25 r4 successor corrected the claims and reassigned the residual rows to their D2 owner.
entries.fix_scope: Append-only r4 successor; r4 lineage itself was later superseded by the round-26 r5 lineage.
entries.before: Earlier revisions retained stale D4 figures and passenger prose.
entries.after: The r4 packet had no stale revision hits and explicitly retained the residual as D2-owned; the r4 checker is historical, not a current checker for r5.
entries.control: Round-25 independent census and checker; round-26 pin-repoint controls and v3 end-to-end successor.
entries.owner_note: Preserve all predecessor revisions. Do not revive or repair the r4 checker against r5 pins; use the successor lineage and its controls.

measurements.result: Exit 0, 52/52 controls; stale-prose detector reported 13 parent hits and zero r4 revision hits.
The r5 successor controls exited 0; pin-repoint controls were 17/17 and the handoff exercise reported 16/16, 20/20, 105/105.

entries.evidence: The stale prose was corrected in a successor, not by rewriting predecessors. The r4 checker is explicitly superseded rather than repaired.

entries.defect: The round-25 gate-input frozen generation pinned an uncommitted working-tree gate digest, so its rows could not replay against a repository object.
entries.fix_scope: Successor manifests pin committed gate bytes; the round-25 generation remains filed unchanged.
entries.before: The round-25 generation's rows refused at gate_digest_mismatch before the gate ran.
entries.after: Later committed generations superseded the uncommitted pin; the round-28 r28-post generation reproduced its recorded rows.
entries.control: Round-26 regression identifies the missing git object; round-28 report records successor replay.
entries.owner_note: Historical generation is superseded, not repaired in place. Keep its expected refusal distinct from current replay status.

measurements.result: Not a valid object name; all six round-25 frozen rows reported gate_digest_mismatch.
Successor generation reproduced 4/4 rows.

entries.evidence: The uncommitted digest was a historical freeze defect. Successor generations are append-only and are not a claim that old rows changed meaning.

entries.defect: The round-26 validation runner passed a nonexistent --root to the r4 checker; exit 2 produced no passed verdict, while the runner recorded a note rather than failing the required checker clause.
entries.owner_note: This is a historical unevaluated check, not a pass or a current product failure. Future required checks must not be satisfied by a receipt with no verdict; do not rewrite the round-26 receipt.

measurements.result: Exit 1 at 18:21:10Z; the checker invoked with --root .scratch/round-26/checker-clone exited 2 because that isolated clone path did not exist, and the receipt contained no passed field.

entries.evidence: Round-26's r4 checker was subsequently superseded by the r5 lineage. The historical runner gap is recorded for future mandatory-check design, not as a need to revive the old checker.

entries.defect: The argot replay gate can accept a base not present as a packet record, a self-derivation, and a wrong derivation after one pair field is deleted; those cases are counted as clean or omitted from replay.
entries.owner_note: Resolve bases to packet records, reject identity derivations unless the declared operation permits them, and HOLD malformed half-pairs. Re-run on the current gate before claiming closure.

measurements.result: A derivation naming a base absent from the packet exited 0 and counted a derived pair.
Palindrome reverse and one-syllable head2 self-derivations exited 0 with zero violations; a bad-pair control exited 1.

measurements.command: python3 tools/gates/argot-derivation-gate.py <A3 fixture with derivation field deleted>
measurements.result: The wrong register-scoped form exited 0 with no finding when one pair field was deleted; the complete pair exited 1.

entries.evidence: The controls isolate three separate identity/scope holes. Later round-27/28 evidence cited here does not establish that these specific attacks were repaired.

entries.defect: The argot leg treats any non-plain register string as argot scope and can replay prose glosses as forms; it does not consult label kind, inventory signature, or borrowed-strata routing.
entries.owner_note: Route by the label-typing table before arithmetic replay. Keep gloss, native-form, borrowed-strata, and argot-register channels distinct; preserve the same-bytes projector control.

measurements.result: A prose gloss on a register slot exited 0 in the argot gate.
The same fixture emitted D2L-NATIVE failure, demonstrating the channel disagreement.
A prose register remained accepted; round-27 review measured the scope/typing gap as not repaired.

entries.evidence: Round-27 reproduced the label-typing gap on full-packet mutations and stated it was reported, not repaired. The clean D4 gate result must not be read as type validation.

entries.defect: Borrow replay applies arbitrary global substitutions to donor_form without requiring declared donor-side correspondence or inventory legality, so an arbitrary one-letter rewrite can be graded as a clean adaptation.
entries.owner_note: Last measured in round 26; current status must be re-probed before treating it as open or closed. Add negative controls for donor correspondence and recipient inventory if the path remains in use.

measurements.result: The arbitrary substitution fixture exited 0 with borrow_pairs=1 and no violations; a mismatching global-rewrite control exited 1.

entries.evidence: The report names an over-permissive borrowed-strata replay rule. This ledger does not assert the same reading on the final round-28 gate without a current re-run.

entries.defect: The argot operation detector scans rule prose for substrings such as reverse and head2, allowing unrelated prose to manufacture a coverage HOLD while synonym phrasing evades the same detector.
entries.owner_note: Last measured in round 26; re-measure the final gate before closure. Operation declarations should be typed fields, not unanchored prose matches.

measurements.result: Three prose variants triggered a manufactured D4L-ARGOT-COVERAGE HOLD; three synonym controls did not.

entries.evidence: The delivered D4 prose did not trigger this false red at that measurement. It is a detector discipline finding, and its present status is unverified.

entries.defect: The argot gate's head2 syllabifier still treats ai/au as two nuclei. The design-correct two-syllable form tumhai is graded red while the gate's truncated tumha reading is green.
entries.owner_note: Fix diphthong syllabification against the packet's declared syllables and design algorithm; retain the opposite-reading probe pair. Do not repeat the superseded cluster-only closure.

measurements.result: Head2 disagreement remained on 3 of 70 forms; the round-27 runner's 0-of-70 reading shared the same diphthong mistake.
The design-correct tumhai form exited 1 with one violation; the gate-reading tumha form exited 0 with zero violations.

entries.evidence: The cluster class was fixed; the diphthong class and its verdict inversion remained explicitly open. Round-28 ceiling prose cites this round-27 correction/supersession record rather than closing the gate residue.

entries.defect: The delivered law gate accepts force values through independent class/modifier substring matches, without checking value membership or polarity; refusals, negation, and fabricated values can pass as valid forces.
entries.owner_note: Declare a machine-readable force vocabulary and grade class, polarity, and qualifiers as related fields. Keep positive and inversion/negation controls; do not self-derive the vocabulary from the values being checked.

measurements.command: python3 - <<'PY' (runpy the delivered tools/gates/register-law-gate.py and test the D18 force probe set)
measurements.result: The delivered gate accepted commissive-binding granted, commissive-binding, not-directive-binding, and none directive naming; the no-such-force control was caught.

measurements.command: python3 - <<'PY' (in-memory RGL-02 force mutation through the delivered gate)
measurements.result: The inverted-force tamper left the clean packet's four dangling-HOLD findings unchanged, while a no-such-force control added a force finding.

entries.evidence: The gate narrowed one none-only case but retained the core substring/polarity overmatch. Round-28 evidence confirms the defect on the delivered gate, not only its review runner.

entries.defect: The delivered law reader misses empty or polarity-inverted consequences and does not resolve bare speaker classes; it resolves only Name (ID) tokens, so a tokenless bogus class is indistinguishable from the clean law row.
entries.owner_note: Validate consequence presence and polarity, and declare/resolve speaker classes explicitly. Add tokenless speaker and consequence-negation controls; do not use a token-bearing speaker fixture as a substitute.

measurements.command: python3 - <<'PY' (in-memory consequence blanking/polarity and tokenless speaker mutations through register-law-gate.py)
measurements.result: Blanked and polarity-inverted consequences and bare bogus speaker classes left the clean finding set unchanged; Name (ID) and no-such-kind controls were caught.

entries.evidence: The round-28 runner's speaker selftest retains an ID token and therefore does not cover the round-27 tokenless speaker-class probe. The gate's stated ID-token limit does not satisfy the stronger claim wording.

entries.defect: The D4 assembler does not validate register_law record fields; stripping an RGL row id still assembles, unlike stripping a lexicon row id.
entries.owner_note: Add register_law to assembler record validation and a mirror-based negative control; keep the lexicon contrast and deterministic-assembly check.

measurements.command: python3 -B tools/assemble-culture-d4.py (isolated full mirror with id stripped from RGL-03)
measurements.result: Exit 0 and emitted a register_law row without id; the same edit to a lexicon row exited 2.

entries.evidence: The component and contract declare fields, but the assembler's record validator lacks a register_law field list. The round-28 mirror control reproduced the asymmetry.

entries.defect: The delivered register-law rows cite QREG-05 through QREG-08, which have no delivered records; the law gate emits clean-packet dangling HOLDs for those citations.
entries.owner_note: Resolve the references by delivering the cited design rows or by correcting the citations in an authorized successor; preserve the HOLD semantics and do not classify the expected clean-packet HOLDs as a gate regression.

measurements.result: The clean packet emitted four D4L-LAW-DANGLING HOLDs for QREG-05..08.

entries.evidence: These are real dangling references, distinct from the gate's expected HOLD semantics and distinct from mutations that should create a new tamper finding.

entries.defect: The delivered register-law gate is not included in the runner's registered regression label set, so its clean exit and tamper controls are not part of the standard battery verdict.
entries.owner_note: Register the law gate in the standard battery with its clean calibration and tamper delta controls; ensure the expected clean-packet dangling HOLDs are interpreted as calibrated baseline, not hidden by omission.

measurements.result: The runner's 35 regression labels contained zero labels naming register-law-gate.py; the separate law gate emitted four clean-packet HOLDs.

entries.evidence: A separate selftest is not a substitute for registration in the standard battery. Round-28 report identifies this as a later-round follow-up.

entries.defect: tools/replay-frozen.py runs a gate whose ROOT resolves to the live repository and loads live peers/packet bytes instead of evaluating only the pinned snapshot; it then classifies the gate's exit-2 refusal as replay_mismatch rather than could-not-evaluate.
entries.owner_note: Build an isolated mirror containing the full pinned read set and dependencies, and preserve an input-class refusal as could-not-evaluate. Keep different pinned inputs from collapsing to the same live-tree output.

measurements.result: At 20:12Z two distinct pinned D4 inputs emitted one identical output digest and exited 2; at 20:26Z their output digests diverged but both still mismatched against live-tree assembly bytes.
The two gate exit-2 refusals were recorded as replay_mismatch/status=mismatch rather than could-not-evaluate.

entries.evidence: The defect predates round 28 and is still reported after the output collision symptom was removed. A matching D2 replay was coincidental because the live D2 bytes equaled its pins.

entries.defect: The round-28 runner's all-replays-green clause checks handoff/selftest labels but excludes frozen-manifest replay, so it can report green while the manifest replay surface is nonzero.
entries.owner_note: Make the acceptance clause enumerate and evaluate the frozen manifest generations it claims to cover; bind refusals and mismatches to separate statuses. Do not infer replay success from handoff selftests.

measurements.result: The replay label set contained replay-selftest and handoff labels but no frozen manifest replay; the sweep recorded 11 of 12 manifest generations as nonzero.

entries.evidence: This is a runner coverage defect independent of replay-frozen's live-tree bug: even a correct replay tool cannot affect a claim clause that never invokes it.

entries.defect: Round-23 through round-28 acceptance runners discover the live lane as an ancestor of an in-lane clone and sync live bytes over the snapshot being measured.
entries.owner_note: Use a clone isolation rule that cannot resolve back to the live lane, or disable synchronization in snapshot-only phases. Require before/after hashes for probe files and keep the current exclusion until repaired.

measurements.result: The passing reproduction changed three HEAD-probe files to their live bytes when reports/round-28/run-validation.py --check ran inside the in-lane clone.

entries.evidence: The round-28 sweep excluded live-syncing runners from the HEAD-only phase, which avoids this contamination in that driver but does not repair the runner behavior.

entries.defect: The round-27 and round-28 gate-test runners parse --check as measure-only but unconditionally write their receipt, so a check-only invocation mutates a filed receipt in the round-27 runner.
entries.owner_note: Make --check read-only and verify receipt hashes before and after; retain the round-27 restored receipt and do not run the writer against filed artifacts in the live lane.

measurements.result: At 17:13:19 direct check-only execution rewrote the filed receipt; it was restored and re-hashed equal to HEAD.
Source inspection and the round-28 regression report confirm the same unconditional receipt write in the successor runner.

entries.evidence: The historical byte was restored, but restoration does not close the writer behavior. The round-28 file was not yet a filed historical artifact when measured.

entries.defect: Family-G sweep admission depends on live-tree lineage instead of the hold set's own packet pin, so a drifted hold set can disappear during the re-pin window; family-J uses a fixed pin-map key vocabulary that misses key families the lane writes.
entries.owner_note: Admit D4 hold sets by their own packet_sha256 against recorded D4 lineage and report drift rather than silently skipping. Extend family-J discovery beyond a fixed key-name list. Do not count historical pin maps as live defects.

measurements.result: At an earlier drift stamp family G returned zero rows; injecting the current hold-set pin made the walker find it. The contemporaneous repair returned one row and the selftest reached 12/12, but the filter remained live-tree-coupled.
The adjudication found pin maps under key names the fixed family-J vocabulary did not read; the historical map census is evidence of key-vocabulary coverage, not a count of live defects.

entries.evidence: The family-G symptom was repaired during the round, but the admission rule still reopens the same blind window on a future packet landing. The static key list is a separate coverage limit.
